lead.headline: Coldcard's $130M+ Firmware Failure Exposes Self-Custody's Fragile Assumptions
lead.tldr: This month's signals reveal a critical tension: institutional infrastructure for tokenized assets is accelerating while the security foundations of Bitcoin self-custody are being stress-tested by exploits that bypass even disciplined user behavior. The market is repricing what 'secure' means.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this month the gap between institutional-grade infrastructure buildout and the fragility of individual security assumptions became impossible to ignore, and it will reshape how we underwrite custody and compliance risk for the next twelve months.

top_signals.title: Harmony plans pre-attack rollback after exploiter forged 3 trillion ONE tokens
top_signals.summary: Harmony is planning a network rollback to recover from a massive exploit where an attacker forged 3 trillion ONE tokens. The protocol determined that a rollback is the most secure and fair method of recovery compared to token burns or wallet blacklisting.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Harmony's planned rollback after a 3 trillion ONE token forge signals that 'finality' remains negotiable in smaller L1s, which reprices recovery risk for any token holder not at the protocol's governance center.

top_signals.title: Coldcard Exploit Abates as Total Losses Climb to (at Least) 1,700 BTC
top_signals.summary: A vulnerability in Coldcard hardware wallets has led to significant losses, with at least 1,700 BTC stolen. While new incidents of the exploit have slowed down, the total amount of lost funds continues to rise as more victims report their losses.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Coldcard exploit's climbing loss count to 1,700 BTC demonstrates that vulnerability discovery is not an event but a process, and post-incident monitoring must be priced into hardware wallet underwriting.

top_signals.title: Why the latest Bitcoin hack hurt more than most
top_signals.summary: A major security breach has resulted in the theft of $100 million from Coldcard hardware wallet users. The incident is particularly significant as it targeted users who followed strict security protocols.
top_signals.why_it_matters: That the Coldcard breach hit users following strict security protocols is the specific fact that kills the thesis that individual operational excellence alone is sufficient custody protection.

top_signals.title: Weekly Research Brief: Coldcard Hacked for $130m+; BTC Price Resilient
top_signals.summary: A major security breach involving Coldcard has resulted in a loss of over $130 million. Despite the exploit, the price of Bitcoin has remained resilient, while Ethereum and Solana are reviewing their inflation schedules.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bitcoin price resilience alongside $130M+ in Coldcard losses shows the market is currently pricing protocol-level security separately from individual custody failures, a dislocation that may not hold as exploit patterns proliferate.

top_signals.title: Inside the COLDCARD Entropy Failure w/ Alex Thorn
top_signals.summary: A critical RNG firmware bug in CoinKite Coldcard hardware wallets has led to an exploit compromising over 1,500 BTC (valued at $100M+). The attack utilized open-source AI models to operationalize the drainer bots, raising concerns about the security of Bitcoin self-custody.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The use of open-source AI models to operationalize Coldcard drainer bots introduces a new variable in custody risk: attacker tooling cost curves are collapsing, which compresses the time window between vulnerability disclosure and mass exploitation.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin owners rocked by $116 million hack: What we know about the Coldcard exploit
top_signals.summary: A massive security breach has targeted Coldcard cold storage wallets, resulting in the theft of 1,816 Bitcoin. The exploit is particularly concerning as it compromised wallets previously considered hyper-secure.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The 1,816 BTC Coldcard theft from 'hyper-secure' wallets reframes the entire hardware wallet category from 'set and forget' to 'continuous firmware verification required.'

top_signals.title: NYSE parent ICE partners with tZERO on infrastructure for tokenized securities
top_signals.summary: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the NYSE, is partnering with tZERO to develop infrastructure for a tokenized securities platform. As part of the agreement, ICE will also participate in tZERO's latest funding round.
top_signals.why_it_matters: ICE's partnership and funding participation in tZERO for tokenized securities infrastructure is the clearest signal yet that regulated incumbents are building parallel rails rather than retrofitting legacy systems.

top_signals.title: Cronos halts network after Tectonic exploit involving estimated $75M33m, Cronos halts network after Tectonic exploit involving estimated $75MCrypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek said the company’s app and exchange were unaffected by the Tectonic breach and continued operating normally.
top_signals.summary: The Cronos network was halted following a security exploit on the Tectonic protocol involving an estimated $75 million. Crypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek clarified that the company's exchange and app remain unaffected and operational.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Cronos halting its entire network after a $75M Tectonic exploit while Crypto.com's centralized operations continued unaffected illustrates the operational divergence risk between DeFi protocols and their associated CeFi brands.

deals.summary: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the NYSE, is partnering with tZERO to develop infrastructure for a tokenized securities platform. As part of the agreement, ICE will also participate in tZERO's latest funding round.
SBI Holdings has invested $270 million to acquire a 20% stake in Ajaib, a digital asset platform. This move is part of SBI's broader strategy to expand its digital asset footprint across Asia.

Kalshi has raised $1.12 billion through private equity offerings since April, according to recent SEC filings. The company is reportedly seeking an additional $750 million in capital at a $40 billion valuation.

Ripple has successfully raised $275 million through a senior note offering to expand its US operations. The funds will be used to develop institutional financial services, specifically focusing on prime brokerage and multi-asset clearing.
Goldman Sachs is acquiring ETF manager NEOS Investments in a deal valued at up to $2.25 billion. This move integrates NEOS's Bitcoin and Ether-linked ETFs into Goldman's asset management division.

Mastercard has finalized the acquisition of BVNK for $1.8 billion to strengthen its stablecoin capabilities. The move aims to provide banks and fintechs with enhanced tools for stablecoin payments, settlements, and treasury services.

BitGo has acquired the institutional trading arm of NYDIG to strengthen its institutional crypto offerings. The deal includes the acquisition of approximately 30 employees and existing client relationships, focusing on expanding derivatives and financing services.

Bitfinex Securities has successfully completed a $50 million tokenized capital raise for Alkemya. The funding was achieved through the issuance of ALKN, a tokenized security representing limited partnership interests.
Stablecoin neobanking platform Fasset has raised $68 million in a Series C funding round led by SBI Group. This investment values the company at $1 billion, marking its transition to unicorn status.

Stripe has agreed to acquire OpenRouter, signaling a strategic move to integrate AI services with crypto-native payment rails. The acquisition reflects a high-conviction bet that the future AI economy will rely on blockchain-based financial infrastructure.

QuantumLight, a venture capital firm co-founded by Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky, has successfully closed its second fund. The fund has raised a total of $500 million to support its investment activities.

on_the_radar.title: Mirae Asset maps out $109 billion digital asset push with Digital X: report
on_the_radar.summary: South Korean financial giant Mirae Asset is planning a massive digital asset expansion centered around its Digital X initiative. The firm aims to build a $109 billion business in the sector with a goal of achieving profitability by 2027.

on_the_radar.title: SEC sends crypto custody rule overhaul to White House for review
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC has sent a proposed overhaul of its decades-old custody requirements to the White House for review. This move, pushed by Paul Atkins, aims to provide clearer regulatory frameworks for the custody of digital assets.

on_the_radar.title: India plans first tokenized bonds using wholesale CBDC: Report20m
on_the_radar.summary: India is planning to launch its first tokenized bonds utilizing a wholesale Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). This move aims to modernize the bond market and improve settlement efficiency through blockchain technology.

on_the_radar.title: Traders bet bitcoin was stuck below $67,000. The Treasury blew that trade up in one afternoon
on_the_radar.summary: A surprise bond buyback by the US Treasury triggered a massive short squeeze in the crypto market. This event liquidated over $4 billion in bearish bets and propelled Bitcoin's price above $77,000.

on_the_radar.title: SEC Proposes Long-Awaited Regulation for Primary Token Issuance
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC has proposed new regulations regarding the primary issuance of digital tokens. While the move aims to provide regulatory clarity, the analysis suggests that durable clarity will ultimately require legislative action from Congress.

on_the_radar.title: View latest issue, $1B Short Squeeze Rockets BTC
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin experienced a significant price surge driven by a $1 billion short squeeze. This event forced short sellers to close their positions, further accelerating the upward price momentum.

on_the_radar.title: Inside the Oval Office meeting: Trump appears ‘bullish’ on Clarity Act as he solicits feedback from crypto, finance CEOs
on_the_radar.summary: President Trump held a private Oval Office meeting with crypto and finance CEOs to solicit feedback on the Clarity Act. Sources indicate the President appears bullish on the passage of the legislation.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin hits $69,000, ether jumps 10% as Treasury buybacks, SEC crypto proposal fuel market rally
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced a significant price rally, with Bitcoin reaching $69,000 and Ether jumping 10%. The surge was driven by Treasury buybacks and a new SEC crypto proposal, resulting in nearly $2 billion in liquidations.

on_the_radar.title: StanChart, HSBC execute first live transaction on Swift blockchain ledger
on_the_radar.summary: Standard Chartered and HSBC have successfully executed the first live cross-border transaction using Swift's blockchain ledger. This milestone marks a significant step in the expansion of tokenized deposit infrastructure among global systemic banks.

on_the_radar.title: SEC proposes new crypto offering rules as Congress stalls on digital asset legislation
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC has proposed a new rule intended to create a formal pathway for investments involving digital assets. This move comes amid a legislative stalemate in Congress regarding digital asset regulation.

on_the_radar.title: Securitize brings Neuberger’s $230 billion fixed-income platform onchain with new tokenized fund
on_the_radar.summary: Securitize is bringing Neuberger Berman's $230 billion fixed-income platform onchain through a new tokenized fund. The HINC fund will be deployed across multiple major blockchains including Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, and Sui.

on_the_radar.title: Citi expects to launch bitcoin custody later this year under its new Custody+ platform
on_the_radar.summary: Citi plans to launch Bitcoin custody services later this year as part of its new Custody+ platform. The platform will integrate AI-powered market intelligence, instant settlements, and liquidity tools.

on_the_radar.title: Tether completes first full financial audit, receives clean KPMG opinion
on_the_radar.summary: Tether has completed its first full independent financial audit for its 2025 financial statements. The audit was conducted by KPMG, which issued a clean opinion on the stablecoin issuer's financials.

on_the_radar.title: SEC clears Franklin Templeton funds to use onchain BENJI system for cash management
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC has issued a no-action letter allowing Franklin Templeton's traditional registered funds to utilize its onchain BENJI system for cash management. This marks a significant step in integrating traditional finance (TradFi) with blockchain-based asset management.

on_the_radar.title: Bank of England tests stablecoin, digital pound interoperability in cross-border payments34m
on_the_radar.summary: The Bank of England is conducting tests to ensure interoperability between a potential digital pound (CBDC) and private stablecoins for cross-border payments. This initiative aims to modernize the UK's payment infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of international settlements.

on_the_radar.title: Wintermute to pour $1B into AI, high-frequency trading amid TradFi expansion: Report28m
on_the_radar.summary: Wintermute plans to invest $1 billion into AI and high-frequency trading as part of its expansion into traditional finance (TradFi). The move signals a strategic push to integrate advanced trading technologies across both crypto and conventional markets.

on_the_radar.title: Fidelity files with SEC to add staking to Ethereum ETF16m, Fidelity files with SEC to add staking to Ethereum ETFFidelity plans to add staking to its Ether fund, with 85% of rewards retained by FETH and quarterly cash distributions planned for investors.
on_the_radar.summary: Fidelity has filed with the SEC to incorporate staking rewards into its Ethereum ETF. The proposal suggests that 85% of rewards would be retained by the fund, with quarterly cash distributions provided to investors.

on_the_radar.title: SEC, CFTC sue Goliath Ventures over $400M crypto Ponzi scheme
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC and CFTC have filed lawsuits against Goliath Ventures in connection with a $400 million cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme. While Delgado has agreed to settle with the SEC, the CFTC is pursuing further penalties and market bans.

worth_a_read.title: SEC Proposes Long-Awaited Regulation for Primary Token Issuance
worth_a_read.note: The SEC's proposed primary token issuance regulation will define the compliance cost structure for any new L1 or protocol token launch, making this required reading for issuance underwriting.

worth_a_read.title: Stripe Agrees to Buy OpenRouter as It Embraces ‘The Singularity’
worth_a_read.note: Stripe's OpenRouter acquisition thesis—that AI services will run on crypto-native payment rails—needs to be stress-tested against actual transaction volume data, and this piece frames the argument to interrogate.

worth_a_read.title: Avalanche Is the Business Chain for Real-World Finance
worth_a_read.note: Avalanche's positioning for real-world finance requires evaluating whether subnet economics can sustain institutional throughput requirements, which this report claims to model.

worth_a_read.title: Exclusive: Nik Storonsky’s VC firm closes $500m for second fund
worth_a_read.note: QuantumLight's $500M close is a datapoint on whether Revolut alumni capital is deploying into crypto-native deals or avoiding the sector, relevant for European early-stage competitive dynamics.

worth_a_read.title: Committing $50M to USHP: The Product Bringing U.S. Home Prices Onchain
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's $50M USHP commitment is a test of whether tokenized real estate can achieve price discovery depth without traditional market maker participation, worth tracking for RWA liquidity assumptions.

worth_a_read.title: How Argentina uses stablecoins, in 5 charts
worth_a_read.note: Argentina's stablecoin usage charts provide the empirical basis for undermining or supporting the 'emerging market demand' narrative that many stablecoin issuers pitch to growth investors.

worth_a_read.title: Coinbase Enters Tokenized Stock Fray on Third-Party ‘Wrapper’ Side
worth_a_read.note: Coinbase's entry into tokenized stocks via wrappers rather than direct issuance reveals strategic positioning around regulatory ambiguity, with implications for how centralized exchanges compete with DEX infrastructure.

worth_a_read.title: The Bull Market Is Back? New Onchain Metas & the GTA VI Hack
worth_a_read.note: The 'bull market is back' framing should be read skeptically against the report's own GTA VI hack detail, which shows how fragile onchain metas remain to external event risk.

linkedin_post: The Coldcard exploit is not a story about user error. 1,816 BTC gone. $130 million plus. These were users who did what they were told: air-gapped hardware, verified addresses, no hot wallet exposure. The attacker used open-source AI to operationalize a firmware RNG bug. That is the specific mechanism that changes the math. Individual operational excellence no longer suffices when attacker tooling costs collapse to near-zero and vulnerability discovery becomes systematic rather than opportunistic. We are repricing what 'secure custody' means, and the market has not caught up. Bitcoin price held. That is the wrong signal to read as resilience. It reads as dislocation. Price discovery at the protocol level has decoupled from individual loss events because the market structure treats these as isolated failures. They are not isolated. They are pattern. Meanwhile ICE is funding tZERO, Goldman is buying NEOS for its ETF infrastructure, Mastercard closed BVNK at $1.8 billion. The institutional buildout assumes custody will be solved. The Coldcard case suggests we are solving for the wrong threat model. What we underwrite a custody provider on today needs to include continuous firmware attestation, not hardware possession. The testable thesis: within eighteen months, either hardware wallet market share concentrates to vendors with real-time vulnerability response, or the category is subsumed by institutional custody layers with insurance-backed SLA structures. I am not certain which path dominates. I am certain the current assumptions are mispriced.
